claims.text: The chicken rice is served with soy-based sauces (black soy / sweet chili); standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat, but no allergen detail is published.
Black coffee, single-origin pour-overs, and roasted beans are naturally free of gluten and animal products, so a plain coffee is a safe choice for most travelers.

name: 珈琲屋 エルムンド (Kohiya El Mundo)

claims.text: Coffee, non-caffeinated teas, and juices can be ordered as plain drinks without dairy or wheat.

name: 糀料理とビオスチームのお店 えん (Koji Ryori to Bio Steam no Omise En)

claims.text: Concept is entirely koji/fermentation-based with house-made fermented seasonings (shio-koji, amazake, miso) and flour-based scones, so gluten-containing ingredients are pervasive throughout the kitchen.
Dishes use house-made fermented seasonings including miso and koji condiments, which in Japanese cooking are typically wheat/barley-inclusive; specific gluten-free formulation is not documented.
The signature plate includes meat and fish marinated in koji and miki served alongside the vegetable and tofu dishes, so animal products are prepared in the same kitchen and on the same plate.
Uses organic, pesticide-free local vegetables and offers genuinely plant-based items such as salt-koji tofu, an 'anti-aging' salad, amazake sweets, and the miki probiotic drink.

Several offerings are simple, rice-based items such as onigiri and tea rice porridge, which can be a gentler starting point for diners avoiding certain ingredients, though specifics must be confirmed in person.

name: ことのま あかり (Kotonoma Akari)

claims.text: Some seasonal sweets are described in local listings as made without dairy or eggs, suggesting the kitchen can sometimes accommodate plant-based requests if asked in advance.

name: ルアン NIPPONIA HOTEL 奈良 ならまち (LE UN NIPPONIA HOTEL Nara Naramachi)

claims.text: Guests with allergies must inform the restaurant either in the comments field at the time of online booking or by phone at least 3 days in advance; due to ingredient preparation, same-day accommodation is not possible.
The restaurant has a stated process for handling allergies when notified at least 3 days ahead of the reservation.

name: メインダイニングルーム「三笠」（奈良ホテル） (Main Dining Room Mikasa (Nara Hotel))

claims.text: All dishes are prepared in the same kitchen, so cross-contamination is possible.
Vegetarian offering is ovo-lacto (includes eggs and dairy) and shares the same kitchen as meat/fish dishes, so cross-contact is possible.
Allergy accommodation is available but requires advance notice when booking.
Offers ovo-lacto vegetarian course options and menus featuring seasonal Yamato vegetables.
